name: dynap_se_64x256x4
display_name: DYNAP-SE (Moradi 2017), 4 cores of 256 neurons x 64 words

faithfulness.note: Geometry only. The registered geometry resolves with its claim class. The description states no pricing, so the label of each run names the pricing the run resolves. A run that declares a physics profile or constants is priced under them, and one that declares neither refuses absolute area, energy and latency by name.

stated.quote: Neuromorphic computing systems comprise networks of neurons that use asynchronous events for both computation and communication.
stated.reads: networks of neurons that use asynchronous events

departs.computation: 2-bit selector of one of 4 synapse circuits whose weights are globally shared biases
departs.location: Section IV 'A multi-core neuromorphic processor prototype', PDF p.8
departs.quote: the 2-bit SRAM memories are used to program the type of synapse circuits to use. Depending on the content of the SRAM a synapse can be programmed to exhibit one of 4 possible behaviors: fast excitatory, slow excitatory, subtractive inhibitory, or shunting inhibitory. Each synapse behavior is modeled by a dedicated DPI circuit, each with globally shared biases that set time constants and weight values.
departs.reads: the 2-bit SRAM memories are used to program the type of synapse circuits to use
departs.reason: The toolchain's weight grid is one symmetric signed integer per synapse. A selector of an analog circuit whose weight is a bias shared across the chip holds no per-synapse integer, so the registered geometry's 2-bit weights (the cell's bits) are assumed in its place.
departs.note: Each synapse word holds a 2-bit SRAM cell that selects one of four synapse circuits of its neuron (Fig. 9 caption, PDF p.9), whose efficacies are analog biases shared per core: the source states no per-synapse integer weight. The registered geometry's 2-bit weights are the description's assumption.

unstated.note: Each synapse word holds one 2-bit SRAM cell, the synapse type's selector: the weight is its neuron's synapse circuit, not a cell count.

stated.quote: Each node comprises 64 mixed memory words, consisting of 10-bit CAM and 2-bit SRAM cells
stated.note: The 2-bit cell selects one of four synapse circuits of its neuron, whose efficacies are analog: the cell's 2 bits are the description's assumed grid, a selector, not a per-synapse integer weight.

unstated.note: A neuron's firing rate can be set by a constant DC current injection (Sec. V), a current the core's bias generators set for a population, not a per-neuron bias; the registered geometry's bias row is the description's assumption.
The neurons are analog adaptive-exponential integrate-and-fire circuits (AdExp-I&F, Sec. IV): no family of the toolchain is that law; a deployment declares one and departs from the chip.
Asynchronous analog dynamics in continuous time: the source states no cycle discipline.
Continuous-time neurons: no spike window is the chip's; the deployment declares it.
Continuous-time neurons: no level count is the chip's; the deployment declares it.
Continuous time: the analog neuron fires when its circuit crosses threshold; no cycle or event compare of the toolchain is stated.
The analog neuron's reset is set by its circuit biases; the source states no reset law in the toolchain's terms.
An analog membrane (a capacitor voltage): no register width.
An analog comparator: no stated compare rule.
